title: "Difference-in-Differences: Canonical 2×2"

  html:
    toc: true

## Setup

We consider the canonical difference-in-differences setup with:
- two groups (treated and control)
- two time periods (before and after treatment)

Treatment affects only the treated group in the post-treatment period.

## The DiD Estimator

The DiD estimator is defined as:

$$
\text{DiD} = (\bar Y_{T,post} - \bar Y_{T,pre}) - (\bar Y_{C,post} - \bar Y_{C,pre})
$$

## Graphical Illustration

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Canonical 2×2 DiD: treatment affects only the treated group after intervention"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)

# Canonical 2x2 DiD data with treatment effect
did_data <- data.frame(
  time = rep(c(0, 1), times = 2),
  group = rep(c("Control", "Treated"), each = 2),
  outcome = c(5, 6, 6, 9)
)

ggplot(did_data, aes(x = time, y = outcome, color = group)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 1),
    labels = c("Before", "After")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Outcome",
    color = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```







## The 2×2 Table and Manual DiD Calculation

We now compute the difference-in-differences estimator using group means.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

did_data <- data.frame(
  time = rep(c(0, 1), times = 2),
  group = rep(c("Control", "Treated"), each = 2),
  outcome = c(5, 6, 6, 9)
)

means <- did_data %>%
  mutate(time = ifelse(time == 0, "Before", "After")) %>%
  group_by(group, time) %>%
  summarise(mean_outcome = mean(outcome), .groups = "drop")

table_2x2 <- pivot_wider(
  means,
  names_from = time,
  values_from = mean_outcome
)

knitr::kable(table_2x2, digits = 2)

delta_treated <- table_2x2$After[table_2x2$group == "Treated"] -
                  table_2x2$Before[table_2x2$group == "Treated"]

delta_control <- table_2x2$After[table_2x2$group == "Control"] -
                  table_2x2$Before[table_2x2$group == "Control"]

did_estimate <- delta_treated - delta_control
did_estimate
```

The difference-in-differences estimate is therefore **2**.

## Inference in Difference-in-Differences

```{r}
#| results: hide
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

did_data <- data.frame(
  outcome = c(5, 6, 6, 9),
  treated = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
  post = c(0, 1, 0, 1)
)

did_data$interaction <- did_data$treated * did_data$post

coef(lm(outcome ~ treated + post + interaction, data = did_data))
```


In the canonical 2×2 design, the DiD regression is fully saturated.
As a result, the treatment effect is exactly identified, but standard errors are not defined.

This illustrates an important point: in the 2×2 case, difference-in-differences is an algebraic identity rather than a statistical model.

Meaningful inference requires additional units or time periods, which we consider in later sections.

## Parallel Trends Assumption

The key identifying assumption underlying difference-in-differences is the parallel trends assumption.

In the absence of treatment, the average outcomes of the treated and control groups would have followed the same time trend.

Formally, the assumption requires:

$$
E[Y_{0t}^T - Y_{0,t-1}^T] = E[Y_{0t}^C - Y_{0,t-1}^C]
$$

where $Y_{0t}$ denotes the potential outcome without treatment.

This assumption is fundamentally untestable, but its plausibility can be assessed using pre-treatment data.

### Graphical Illustration of Parallel Trends

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Parallel trends before treatment and divergence after treatment"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)

pt_data <- data.frame(
  time = rep(-2:1, times = 2),
  group = rep(c("Control", "Treated"), each = 4),
  outcome = c(4, 5, 6, 7, 5, 6, 7, 10)
)

ggplot(pt_data, aes(x = time, y = outcome, color = group)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Outcome", color = "Group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
